segments.speaker: agent
segments.text_original: Hello Marcus, this is Jordan from OPSWAT support. I have your case about MetaDefender Core not starting after the upgrade. Can you tell me what happened?

segments.speaker: customer
segments.text_original: Hi Jordan. We upgraded Core last night. Since then the Core service starts, but about ten seconds later it stops again, and the web console never loads.

segments.speaker: agent
segments.text_original: Understood. Is this a Windows server, and which version of Core did you upgrade to?

segments.speaker: customer
segments.text_original: Yes, Windows Server. We went from 5.10.1 to 5.13.2, and the installer reported success at the end.

segments.speaker: agent
segments.text_original: Thank you. Is there anything in the Core log from the moment it stops?

segments.speaker: customer
segments.text_original: Let me look. The last lines say failed to start the web service, address already in use, port 8008. Then the service shuts itself down.

segments.speaker: agent
segments.text_original: That usually means another process is already listening on that port. Did you stop the old Core service before the upgrade, and has anything else been installed on that server?

segments.speaker: customer
segments.text_original: I believe the installer stopped it for us. Nothing else has been installed on that server. The services list only shows the one Core service.

segments.speaker: agent
segments.text_original: While Core is stopped, could you list what is listening on port 8008, together with the process ID?

segments.speaker: customer
segments.text_original: One moment. Okay, there is a process listening on 8008 with ID 4312. In the task manager it looks like an old Core worker process, started yesterday before the upgrade.

segments.speaker: agent
segments.text_original: That would explain it. A leftover process from the old version may be holding the port, so the new service cannot start. I have not confirmed whether the installer should have stopped it, so I will check the upgrade documentation and ask our engineering team.

segments.speaker: customer
segments.text_original: Can I simply end that process and start the service again?

segments.speaker: agent
segments.text_original: Since it is an old Core process, ending it and then starting the Core service is reasonable. Please tell me whether the service stays running, and keep the Core log in case it stops again.

segments.speaker: customer
segments.text_original: Okay, I will do that right after this call and report back. I will also attach the installer log from last night.

segments.speaker: agent
segments.text_original: Thank you. I will send the steps for stopping the services cleanly before an upgrade, and follow up on the leftover process. Thanks, Marcus.
